title: Spelling-change -er verbs: j'achète, nous commençons
summary: Some -er verbs change spelling with je, tu, il and ils (j'achète, j'appelle, je paie) or with nous (nous commençons).
focus: Spelling changes in -er verbs in the present: the boot pattern, ç and -yer
content:
## The boot pattern

Some -er verbs change their spelling in the present, always in the same four places: **je**, **tu**, **il / elle / on** and **ils / elles**. Draw a line around those four in the table and you get the shape of a boot; **nous** and **vous** stay outside it and keep the infinitive's spelling.

| | acheter (to buy) |
|---|---|
| je / j' | **achète** |
| tu | **achètes** |
| il / elle / on | **achète** |
| nous | achetons |
| vous | achetez |
| ils / elles | **achètent** |

Why? Inside the boot the ending is silent, so the vowel before it carries the voice and sounds open, like **è**. With **-ons** and **-ez** the ending is heard and that vowel stays light. The endings themselves are the regular ones: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent.

## E → è and é → è

Two families put a grave accent in the boot:

| | acheter | préférer |
|---|---|---|
| je / j' | achète | préfère |
| tu | achètes | préfères |
| il / elle / on | achète | préfère |
| nous | achetons | préférons |
| vous | achetez | préférez |
| ils / elles | achètent | préfèrent |

- Like **acheter**: **se promener** (to go for a walk): **je me promène**, **nous nous promenons**.
- Like **préférer**: **espérer** (to hope): **j'espère**; **répéter** (to repeat): **il répète**.

In **préférer** only the second **é** changes: **je préfère**, never *je prèfère*.

## Doubling: appeler and jeter

**Appeler** (to call) and **jeter** (to throw) double their consonant in the boot instead of taking an accent:

| | appeler | jeter |
|---|---|---|
| je / j' | appelle | jette |
| tu | appelles | jettes |
| il / elle / on | appelle | jette |
| nous | appelons | jetons |
| vous | appelez | jetez |
| ils / elles | appellent | jettent |

The double **ll** or **tt** does the same job as **è**: it makes the **e** before it sound open. You already know one of these forms: **je m'appelle** comes from **s'appeler**, the same verb with **se**.

## -cer, -ger and -yer

These verbs change to keep a sound:

- **-cer**: only the **nous** form changes. A **c** before **o** would sound like **k**, so it takes a cedilla: **nous commençons** (we begin), **nous avançons** (we move forward).
- **-ger** (recap): **nous mangeons**, **nous voyageons** keep an **e** so the **g** stays soft.
- **-yer**: the **y** becomes **i** in the boot: **je paie**, **tu paies**, **ils paient**, but **nous payons**, **vous payez**. Same for **envoyer** (to send): **j'envoie**, and **essayer** (to try): **j'essaie**.

With **-ayer** verbs, keeping the **y** is also correct: **je paye**, **j'essaye**. The drill uses **je paie**.

vocabulary.example: Ma mère achète le journal tous les matins.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My mother buys the newspaper every morning.

vocabulary.example: Mes grands-parents se promènent après le déjeuner.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandparents go for a walk after lunch.

vocabulary.example: Mes enfants préfèrent les vacances à la mer.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My children prefer holidays by the sea.

vocabulary.example: Nous espérons visiter Paris cet été.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We hope to visit Paris this summer.

vocabulary.example: Vous répétez la phrase, s'il vous plaît ?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Can you repeat the sentence, please?

vocabulary.meaning: to call (on the phone, or by name)
vocabulary.example: Le soir, j'appelle souvent ma sœur.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In the evening, I often call my sister.

vocabulary.example: Nous jetons les vieux papiers.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We throw away the old papers.

vocabulary.example: Le concert commence à neuf heures.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The concert begins at nine.

vocabulary.example: Mon père paie toujours le restaurant.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My father always pays for the restaurant.

vocabulary.example: Ma grand-mère envoie des cartes postales.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandmother sends postcards.

quiz.prompt: Nous ___ du pain tous les matins. (acheter)
quiz.explanation: Nous is outside the boot, so it keeps the infinitive's spelling, with no accent: nous achetons.

quiz.prompt: Moi, je ___ le thé au café. (préférer)
quiz.explanation: Je is inside the boot: the second é becomes è. Je préfère.

quiz.prompt: Which spelling of appeler is right for 'they call'?
quiz.explanation: Ils is inside the boot, so appeler doubles its l: ils appellent. Only nous appelons and vous appelez keep one l.
hints: Appeler doubles a letter instead of taking an accent.

quiz.prompt: Nous ___ le cours à neuf heures. (commencer)
quiz.explanation: Before -ons, the c needs a cedilla to keep its s sound: nous commençons.
hints: The c must still sound like s before o.

quiz.prompt: In the boot pattern, nous and vous keep the spelling of the infinitive: nous achetons, vous achetez.
quiz.explanation: The change happens only with je, tu, il / elle / on and ils / elles. Nous and vous have audible endings and keep the infinitive's spelling.
hints: Which four persons make the boot?

quiz.prompt: Tu ___ par carte ou en espèces ? (payer)
quiz.explanation: Tu is inside the boot, so the y of payer becomes i: tu paies (tu payes is also correct).
hints: The y becomes i with tu.
Pays is a noun: a country.

quiz.prompt: Elle ___ ses vieux journaux à la poubelle. (jeter)
quiz.explanation: Elle is inside the boot, so jeter doubles its t: elle jette.
hints: Like appeler, jeter doubles its consonant.

quiz.prompt: Le professeur ___ la question deux fois. (répéter)
quiz.explanation: Répéter works like préférer: the second é becomes è inside the boot. Il répète.

quiz.prompt: 'Nous mangons' is spelt correctly, like 'nous parlons'.
quiz.explanation: In -ger verbs, nous keeps an e so the g stays soft: nous mangeons.
hints: What does g sound like before o?

conversations.title: Planning a party
conversations.scenario: Léa and Sami share out the shopping and the phone calls for a party at their flat on Saturday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pour la fête de samedi, qui achète les boissons ?
lines.meaning: For Saturday's party, who's buying the drinks?
lines.note: il form inside the boot: achète

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: J'achète les boissons. Et toi, tu achètes le gâteau ?
lines.meaning: I'll buy the drinks. And you, will you buy the cake?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: D'accord. Tu préfères un gâteau au chocolat ou aux fraises ?
lines.meaning: OK. Do you prefer a chocolate cake or a strawberry one?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Je préfère le chocolat, mais Paul préfère les fraises.
lines.meaning: I prefer chocolate, but Paul prefers strawberries.
lines.note: only the second é becomes è

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Alors j'achète deux gâteaux ! On commence à quelle heure ?
lines.meaning: Then I'll buy two cakes! What time do we start?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Nous commençons à huit heures. J'appelle Paul et Sarah ce soir.
lines.meaning: We start at eight. I'll call Paul and Sarah tonight.
lines.note: ç before -ons; ll in the boot

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Et moi, j'envoie un message aux voisins.
lines.meaning: And I'll send a message to the neighbours.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Bonne idée. Et les pizzas, qui paie ?
lines.meaning: Good idea. And the pizzas, who's paying?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Nous payons ensemble, c'est plus simple.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Parfait. J'espère qu'il va faire beau !
lines.meaning: Perfect. I hope the weather will be nice!

listening.meaning: On Sundays, we go for a walk in the park.
listening.note: New word: le parc = the park.

listening.note: New word: la copine = the girlfriend.

guide.tip: Listen to the verb: whenever the ending is silent (je, tu, il, ils), the e or é before it sounds like è. Write what you hear: è, ll or tt.

concept.title: Je paie or je paye?
concept.markdown: Verbs in **-ayer** (**payer**, **essayer**) may keep their **y**: **je paye** and **j'essaye** are as correct as **je paie** and **j'essaie**. Verbs in **-oyer** and **-uyer** (**envoyer**, **nettoyer**, **s'ennuyer**) must change: **j'envoie**, never *j'envoye*.

bites.title: The boot
bites.rule: Spelling changes happen with je, tu, il and ils only. Nous and vous keep the infinitive's spelling: j'achète but nous achetons.
bites.example: J'achète du pain, nous achetons du fromage.
bites.example_meaning: I buy bread, we buy cheese.

bites.title: E or é becomes è
bites.rule: Acheter, se promener: e → è. Préférer, espérer, répéter: the last é → è. Only inside the boot.
bites.example: Je préfère le thé, vous préférez le café.
bites.example_meaning: I prefer tea, you prefer coffee.

bites.title: Double the consonant
bites.rule: Appeler and jeter double their l or t inside the boot: j'appelle, ils jettent; but nous appelons, vous jetez.
bites.example: Elle appelle sa mère tous les soirs.
bites.example_meaning: She calls her mother every evening.

bites.title: ç, ge and i
bites.rule: Nous commençons (ç before o), nous mangeons (ge before o). -yer: y → i in the boot: je paie, nous payons.
bites.example: Nous commençons à huit heures et je paie le café.
bites.example_meaning: We start at eight and I'm paying for the coffee.

sorts.title: Inside or outside the boot?
sorts.why: Je, tu, il and ils have silent endings and change; nous and vous keep the infinitive's spelling.

sorts.title: Which change?
sorts.why: Acheter and se promener take è; préférer and espérer turn their last é into è; appeler and jeter double; -yer verbs turn y into i.

spots.why: Nous is outside the boot: no accent.
Inside the boot, the second é becomes è.
Appeler doubles its l with il.
C before o needs a cedilla: ç.
Vous keeps the y of payer.
Ils is inside the boot: double t.

builds.meaning: I buy bread in the morning.

realm.content:
## Les achats à Eldmark

Before a quest, the party shops in Highgate: **j'achète une potion**, **nous achetons des flèches**. Borin **préfère** l'épée; **nous préférons** l'arc. The dwarf **paie** in gold, **nous payons** together, and **nous commençons** la quête at dawn. The boot again: je, tu, il, ils change; nous and vous don't.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The paladin buys a shield.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Elves prefer the forest.

bites.title: Avant la quête
bites.rule: Boot verbs at the market: j'achète, tu achètes, il achète, ils achètent, but nous achetons, vous achetez. Payer too: je paie, nous payons.
bites.example: Nous achetons des flèches, et Borin paie.
bites.example_meaning: We buy arrows, and Borin pays.

listening.meaning: I'm buying a wooden bow.
We pay in gold coins.

spots.why: Nous is outside the boot: one t.

sorts.title: Which spelling?
sorts.why: Inside the boot (je, tu, il, ils) the spelling changes; nous and vous keep the infinitive.

quiz.prompt: La mage ___ un sort à l'orc. (jeter)
quiz.explanation: Elle (la mage) is inside the boot, so jeter doubles its t: elle jette un sort.
Nous is outside the boot, so payer keeps its y: nous payons.

meadowbrook.content:
## Les courses à Meadowbrook

On market day, **j'achète du beurre** and **nous achetons des graines** at Rosa's. Nora **préfère** les fraises; **nous préférons** le maïs. **Nous commençons** la récolte in autumn, and Léo **appelle** ses poules. The boot again: je, tu, il, ils change; nous and vous keep the infinitive.

vocabulary.example: Nora achète des graines à la graineterie.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora buys seeds at the seed shop.

vocabulary.example: Les vaches préfèrent l'herbe près de la rivière.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The cows prefer the grass near the river.

vocabulary.example: Léo appelle ses poules le matin.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Léo calls his hens in the morning.

vocabulary.example_meaning: We start the harvest in autumn.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa sends flowers to the mayor.

vocabulary.example_meaning: The customers pay at the market.

vocabulary.example: Le dimanche, nous nous promenons au bord de la rivière.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa sells sunflower seeds.

bites.example_meaning: We start the harvest, and Nora buys butter.

sorts.title: Which change?
sorts.why: Acheter and se promener take è, appeler and jeter double, payer and envoyer turn y into i.

quiz.explanation: Nora (elle) is inside the boot: acheter takes è. Nora achète des graines.

quiz.prompt: 'Nous commençons la récolte' needs the ç so the c still sounds like s before o.
quiz.explanation: Without the cedilla, c before o sounds like k. Nous commençons keeps the s sound.

rustwake.content:
## Les échanges à Rustwake

At the scrap market, **je paie** in nuts, but **nous payons** together. Marta **préfère** les vieilles piles; **nous préférons** l'eau filtrée. On the radio-montre, **j'appelle** Léo and **j'envoie** un signal. **Nous commençons** l'exploration at dawn. The boot: je, tu, il, ils change; nous and vous keep the infinitive.

vocabulary.example: Je paie l'eau filtrée en écrous.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I pay for the filtered water in nuts.

vocabulary.example: Marta préfère les écrous neufs.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta prefers new nuts.

vocabulary.example: J'appelle le contremaître à la radio-montre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I call the foreman on the wrist radio.

vocabulary.example: L'antenne envoie un signal au Dôme.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The antenna sends a signal to the Dome.

vocabulary.example: Nous espérons trouver de l'eau.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We hope to find water.

vocabulary.example: Le robot jardinier jette la vieille ferraille.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The gardener robot throws away the old scrap.

vocabulary.example: Nous commençons l'exploration demain.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We start the exploration tomorrow.

vocabulary.example: Le village est plein de ferraille.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The village is full of scrap metal.

vocabulary.example: La radio-montre marche avec une pile.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The wrist radio runs on a battery.

vocabulary.example: Le signal est faible aujourd'hui.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The signal is weak today.

bites.title: Au marché de ferraille
bites.rule: Trade with boot verbs: je paie, tu paies, ils paient, but nous payons, vous payez. Acheter too: j'achète, nous achetons.
bites.example: Je paie en écrous, mais vous payez en eau.
bites.example_meaning: I pay in nuts, but you pay in water.

listening.meaning: Marta buys batteries.
listening.note: New word: la pile = the battery.

listening.meaning: They throw the scrap metal outside.
listening.note: New word: la ferraille = the scrap metal.

listening.text: Nous envoyons un signal ce soir.
listening.meaning: We're sending a signal tonight.
listening.note: New word: le signal = the signal.

sorts.title: Boot or not?
sorts.why: Je, tu, il and ils change the spelling; nous and vous keep the infinitive's.

quiz.prompt: Marta asks: 'Vous ___ en écrous ou en eau ?' (payer)
quiz.explanation: Vous is outside the boot, so payer keeps its y: vous payez.

quiz.prompt: Chaque soir, l'antenne ___ un signal au Dôme. (envoyer)
quiz.explanation: L'antenne (elle) is inside the boot: the y of envoyer becomes i. Elle envoie.
hints: -oyer verbs always change y to i in the boot.
